reasoning.argument: For adjacent core tiles, pair equality gives \((b_x,c_x)=(a_{x+1},b_{x+1})\), so internal neighbors coincide with the north word. The external pair boundaries supply exactly the two wall neighbors. A wall in an internal neighbor position would force a north center outside \(A\), which is impossible. At \(W=1\), the two supplied neighbors are both walls.
reasoning.conclusion: Sound under the stated typed-color conventions.

reasoning.argument: Induct on one-head rows. The head-centered tile either writes the new headed symbol for displacement zero or writes the new plain symbol. Exactly the destination neighbor acquires the new head; all other plain centers remain unchanged. Undefined transitions or an outward move remove the required head-centered tile. Thus an existing complete core row is exactly one in-strip step and preserves one-head validity.
reasoning.conclusion: Sound conditional generic local-rule argument, not an evaluated transition table.

reasoning.argument: Disjoint pair/seen horizontal colors force each nontrivial-width row to be entirely core or collector. For width one, the bottom and vertical colors give the same conclusion without an adjacency assumption. Every collector emits stop, and no tile north reads stop, so the only possible collector is the last row; the stop bottom forces it there. Its flags begin zero, change exactly once on an accepting head, and finish one. Headless, second-head and nonaccepting-head rows cannot match.

The first \(H\) rows are core rows. Pair recovery plus the local step induction yields the unique in-strip \(H\)-step run. The final collector establishes acceptance. Conversely, a genuine such run supplies every core triple and the unique seen progression. With \(H=0\), the collector reads the specified initial row directly; it accepts exactly an already accepting row.
reasoning.conclusion: Conditional equivalence supported by the prose proof.

reasoning.argument: The four-state grammar permits exactly left blanks, one head/start cell, binary public bits, separator, binary unknown certificate bits, end marker and right blanks. Pinned head/start, all public bits and the immediately following separator force the declared public word. The proof word and its length remain choices. Distinct fixed-top/top-grammar center roles are essential; they select from one fixed inventory rather than supplying a target proof.
reasoning.conclusion: No public-prefix or fixed-top bypass found under the required role assignments.

reasoning.argument: Each allowed placement has singleton unit positive support at a required center. Capacity one selects one prototype there. Adjacent even centers share exactly the appropriate midpoint in channel \(V\) or \(H\); distinct channels prevent corner/selector interference. Required selector centers, fixed side flags and bottom stop reproduce the finite boundary relations. The master permits finite required sets and explicit admissible origins, so this does not assert coverage of every point of \(\mathbb Z^2\).
reasoning.conclusion: Faithful finite required-point encoding conditional on complete prototype role assignments.

reasoning.argument: Each fixed board has a finite complete placement universe and finite assignments. A finite accepting run has finite tape footprint; translating the start with adequate left padding fits some \((W,H,\ell)\). Enumeration by total size eventually reaches it. An implementation must finish each finite search or dovetail fairly; runtime cutoffs, learned restrictions or finite-board failure never establish non-theoremhood.

specification.central_claim: For any one fixed finite deterministic TM table satisfying the declared machine convention, its specified finite Wang tile family represents exactly the finite in-strip computation prefixes from a valid one-head initial row; the separate collector accepts exactly accepting final configurations. This generic compilation lemma has a mathematical proof sketch in review.html, not a mechanized proof. It is not a newly discovered source theorem or an implemented universal proof system.

conditional_lemma.parameters: One frozen finite table \(\delta\); \(W\ge1\); \(H\ge0\); and a fixed valid one-head \(C_0\in A^W\).
conditional_lemma.proof_status: Own standard mathematical derivation for independent review; no proof assistant, checker, simulator, example table or execution. No novelty or performance claim.
proof_steps: Horizontal pair matching forces every tile triple to be the left/current/right neighbors of its north row, with wall only at strip ends.
The local \(F\) cases agree with exactly one legal \(\delta\) step on a one-head row. Escape or a halt makes the head-centered tile absent. One-head validity is preserved.
Vertical cell colors compose those rows, establishing finite-strip soundness by induction. A genuine in-strip run supplies every triple tile, establishing completeness.

The collector flag begins at zero, changes to one exactly on an accepting head, and ends at one; it therefore requires exactly one accepting head and rejects every other head. Conversely such a row supplies a compatible seen-flag progression.
conditional_lemma.statement_latex: \(\text{the specified }W\times(H+1)\text{ accepting rectangle exists}\iff C_0\text{ has an in-strip }H\text{-step run ending in }q_{\mathrm{acc}}\)

exact_point_model.arithmetic: Exact integer coordinates and unit capacities; finite injective integer codes for typed colors. Value transforms are identity under translations.
exact_point_model.channels: V at north/south, H at west/east, R for center role. Only declared components are assigned; other components are absent (*), never silently assigned zero.
exact_point_model.equivalence_argument: Unit center occupancy selects exactly one role-compatible prototype at each target center. Equality at each shared edge midpoint is exactly the relevant Wang edge match. In top-fixed mode, public clamps fix arbitrary specified \(C_0\); in top-grammar mode, the automaton plus public pins selects exactly the declared initial language. Every finite Wang solution with its chosen top mode extends to selectors, and every exact point solution restricts to that boundary-conditioned Wang solution.
exact_point_model.fixed_background: Roles and public source-word pins are problem-defining markings and are part of the requested finite instance. They are not learned acceleration constraints.
exact_point_model.scope: Finite required centers with explicit boundary data and restricted allowed origins, translations only. This does not establish an unconstrained whole-plane tiling, an aperiodic tile set, or an implemented point-search engine.
selector_families: Left role selector assigns its east \(H\) component one of the wall/current pair colors, or the assigned seen-zero color.
Right role selector assigns its west \(H\) component one of the current/wall pair colors, or the assigned seen-one color.
Each bottom selector assigns its north \(V\) component stop.

For each \(b\in A\), a fixed-top selector has role top-fixed and assigns only its south \(V\) component the cell color \(b\). For the known-row lemma all those shared vertical colors are clamped to \(C_0\).

Top-grammar selectors are the fixed automaton-transition family; they assign south \(V\) and west/east init states. Distinct top roles prevent the fixed-top family from bypassing the unknown-certificate grammar.

The two top-corner selectors assign the initial left and final right automaton states. They enforce the grammar in top-grammar mode and impose no extra condition on fixed-top selectors whose horizontal components are absent.
Unused selector edge components are genuinely absent; selectors are explicit boundary point objects, not a claim of a completed uniform-plane Wang boundary gadget.
exact_point_model.target: Every center in \(B\cup Q_{\mathrm{sel}}\) is required at total \(t\)-value one. All placements have their center in this finite declared target; tile types remain fixed. A problem-defining background role marking assigns bulk, left, right, top-fixed, top-grammar, bottom, init-left or init-right to the corresponding centers. The chosen top mode is uniform across that row.
exact_point_model.top_mode_is_data_not_new_grammar: Both finite top-selector families belong to the same fixed prototype inventory. The finite background selects a mode; no machine table, tile family or proof-step grammar is regenerated per theorem.

machine_convention.fixedness_policy: Once the intended checker is compiled, Gamma, Q, delta, all tile prototypes, color encodings, boundary grammar and source-theory/kernel policy must be frozen once for all target statements. A different statement or candidate proof changes boundary data and finite bounds, never the machine table or tile grammar. Changing the checker/theory policy creates a new system version.
machine_convention.halting_convention: \(\delta\) is undefined on every accepting-state pair. Other undefined transitions are nonaccepting halts. A step writes the symbol, changes state, then moves by its declared displacement; zero displacement keeps the head on the written cell.
machine_convention.head_encoding: plain(s) and head(q,s) are disjoint tagged forms; wall is an additional sentinel outside A.
machine_convention.strip: Width \(W\ge1\), with cells indexed from \(0\) through \(W-1\). The wall sentinel occurs only as the neighbor just outside either end. A valid configuration has exactly one head.

partial_radius_one_update.boundary: \(F\) is a partial function on a finite domain. These formal cases are mathematical data, not an implemented/evaluated CA, TM simulator, compiler or rule table.

The central component is a head moving left with \(a=\#\) or right with \(c=\#\).
